extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/formatting requirements for handling requests, petitions, patent owner statements, and amendments in ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO (per MPEP and 37 CFR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner informs >CRU Supervisory Patent Examiner (SPE)< of intent to issue an order denying reexamination; the CRU SPE will convene a panel review conference (see MPEP §2271.01). If the conference confirms the examiner’s preliminary decision to deny, the proposed order shall be issued and signed by the examiner with two other conferees initialing the action (as 'conferee'). If the conference does not confirm the preliminary decision, the examiner will reevaluate and issue an appropriate communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MPEP §2271.01 for panel makeup. Conferees initial to indicate presence. If panel disagrees, examiner must reconsider rather than issue denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A request raises a 'substantial new question of patentability' when cited prior art teaches something not present in prosecution of the patent, and there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the teaching important in deciding patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the reference's teaching was present in the original prosecution and whether it would be important to a reasonable examiner. Example: Smith teaching spring-supported extruder at 30° raised SNQ for Claims 1–3 because that teaching was not in the prosecution and could be important to patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not requested are not reexamined
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for which reexamination has not been requested will not be reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify which claims are part of the reexamination order. Example language: 'reexamination has not been requested for claims 5–20 ... will not be reexamined.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Time extensions: 37 CFR 1.136 vs 1.550
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) (applicable to 'an applicant') are not permitted in reexamination proceedings; reexamination proceedings are conducted with 'special dispatch' under 37 CFR 1.550(a), and extensions are governed by 37 CFR 1.550(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply applicant-only extension rules (1.136) to reexamination participants; follow 1.550(c) for permissible extensions in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner continuing duty to apprise Office (37 CFR 1.565(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner is reminded of the continuing responsibility under 37 CFR 1.565(a) to apprise the Office of any litigation activity, or other prior or concurrent proceeding, involving the patent throughout the course of the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners must report litigation or other proceedings affecting the patent during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition from denial under 37 CFR 1.515(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requester may seek review by a petition to the Director under §1.181 within one month of the mailing date of the examiner’s determination refusing ex parte reexamination; any such petition must comply with §1.181(b). If no petition is timely filed or if the petition decision affirms no SNQ, the determination is final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is strict (one month). Petition must follow §1.181(b) formatting and grounds rules. A decision affirming denial is final and nonappealable per 35 U.S.C. 303(c) and 37 CFR 1.515(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU jurisdiction while petition period open
rubrics_metrics.description: After denial, the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) retains jurisdiction over the reexamination proceeding to await the possibility of a petition seeking review; if no petition is filed within one month, the CRU will process the reexamination file as a concluded reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat the file as concluded until the petition window has closed or a petition decision finalizes the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU Director review and reassignment when petition granted
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition is filed, it is forwarded to the CRU Director for de novo review of the examiner’s determination. If the petition is granted, the decision should set a 2-month period for filing a statement under 37 CFR 1.530; the reexamination file will then be returned to the CRU SPE for consideration of reassignment to another examiner. Reassignment will be the general rule; only in exceptional circumstances will the case remain with the examiner who denied the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reassignment avoids prior involvement bias; permitted exceptions are narrow (e.g., only examiners available with necessary technical knowledge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner statement timing (37 CFR 1.530(a)/(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in §1.510(e), no statement or other response by the patent owner in an ex parte reexamination shall be filed prior to the determinations made in accordance with §1.515 or §1.520. If a premature statement is filed, it will not be acknowledged or considered and will be returned or discarded (at the Office's option). The order for ex parte reexamination will set a period of not less than two months within which the patent owner may file a statement and any proposed amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file a 1.530 statement before SNQ/grant/deny determination (except per 1.510(e)). The statutory minimum from order to statement is two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required in patent owner statement (37 CFR 1.530(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any statement filed by the patent owner shall clearly point out why the subject matter as claimed is not anticipated or rendered obvious by the prior art patents or printed publications, either alone or in any reasonable combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements must specifically address anticipation/obviousness over each cited reference and combinations; where a third-party requester filed the request, the owner’s statement must be served on the requester per §1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and limits on extensions for patent owner statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the 2-month period is the minimum provided by statute, first extensions may be granted up to one month based upon good and sufficient reasons. Further extensions should be granted only in the most extraordinary situations (e.g., death or incapacitation of representative or owner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant extensions carefully; document 'good and sufficient reasons' for first extension and reserve further extensions for exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service requirement and remedy for omission
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the statement must be served by the patent owner on the requester, unless the request was filed by the patent owner. Lack of proof of service poses a problem; the Reexamination Clerk should contact the patent owner to request supplemental proof or contact the requester to verify service. If proof of service is not provided, the patent owner’s statement may be considered inappropriate and may be denied consideration (see MPEP §2267).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure service and proof of service accompany the owner's statement; failure leads to administrative follow-up and possible denial of consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner waiver of statement to expedite (37 CFR 1.550(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent owner has determined that a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 will not be filed, the patent owner may expedite the proceeding by filing a paper indicating that the patent owner waives the filing of a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 and serving the waiver on the requester, if any. This permits reexamination to proceed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.550(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal waiver plus service expedites the process; file and serve properly to trigger 1.550(a) handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: General manner of making amendments in reexamination (37 CFR 1.530(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed amendment is made by filing a paper directing specified changes to the patent specification (including claims) or drawings. Amendments may accompany an owner request under §1.510(e), be part of a patent owner statement under paragraph (b), or be submitted during prosecution under §1.550(a) or §1.937.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §1.530(d) pathways for timing of when amendments may be submitted; adhere to formal presentation rules in §1.52.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendment format (37 CFR 1.530(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification (other than the claims) must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph including markings pursuant to paragraph (f) (brackets/underlining), except that an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presentation of its text. The precise point in the specification must be identified where any added or rewritten paragraph is located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit full paragraph text with bracketing/underlining; identify insertion points; requirement applies irrespective of filing medium (paper or CD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims amendment requirements (37 CFR 1.530(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each patent claim being changed and of each new claim proposed. For any claim changed, a parenthetical 'amended', 'twice amended', etc., should follow the claim number. Proposed new claims must be underlined throughout. A canceled claim may be canceled by direction without presenting the claim text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present whole claim text with markings; mark 'amended' parenthetically; new claims underlined; canceled claims may be indicated by cancellation statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for reexamination amendments (37 CFR 1.530(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes relative to the patent being reexamined must show matter to be omitted enclosed in brackets and matter to be added underlined. All bracketing and underlining is made in comparison to the original patent (not to prior amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single brackets for deletions and underlining for additions; compare to original patent text when applying markings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering preserved (37 CFR 1.530(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered. A patent claim retains its number even if it is canceled in the reexamination proceeding, and the numbering of any added claims must begin after the last original patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not renumber existing claims; assign numbers for added claims sequentially after the highest original claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of disclosure to secure correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may require specification amendments to ensure support for claim changes and internal consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope or new matter (37 CFR 1.530(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent. Amendments will not be effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject amendments that broaden claims or introduce new matter (see 35 U.S.C. 305 and MPEP §2258). Even accepted amendments are not effective until certificate issuance; expired patents cannot be broadened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for papers (37 CFR 1.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers to become part of USPTO records must be on uniform-size sheets (A4 or 8.5x11), unbound, flexible, white, single-sided, with specified margins (top ≥2.0 cm, left ≥2.5 cm, right ≥2.0 cm, bottom ≥2.0 cm), typed or machine-printed in permanent dark ink, with sufficient clarity/contrast. Specifications must be 1.5 or double spaced, nonscript font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, Courier) preferably size 12 (but not smaller than 0.08 inch), single column; claims and abstract must begin on separate physical/electronic pages. Electronic filings must comply with Office electronic filing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow all 1.52(a)/(b) formalities strictly. See §§1.58 and 1.84 for formulas/tables and drawings formatting. Avoid holes in sheets; pre-printed Office forms exceptions noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing proposed changes in red for examiner approval. Upon approval, new sheets with changes and in compliance with §1.84 must be filed. Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended', new figures as 'New', and canceled figures surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit redline sketch separately; update drawings formally only after examiner approval and follow 1.84 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims and support for claim changes (37 CFR 1.530(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims, there must be supplied, on separate pages from the changes, the status (i.e., pending or canceled) as of the date of the amendment for all patent claims and added claims, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes to the claims made by the amendment paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit claim status generally results in an informal response (see MPEP §2266.02) and may lead to non-entry if submitted after final rejection. The support explanation is critical to meritorious consideration (see MPEP §2266.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments in reexamination require full text and markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner’s amendments made at the time the Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) is prepared require the full text of any paragraph or claim to be changed, with markings; the exception for examiner’s amendment in 37 CFR 1.121(g) does not apply to examiner’s amendments in reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat examiner amendments in reexamination with the same full-text-and-markings requirements as owner amendments; do not rely on 1.121(g) exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings compared to original patent, not prior amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: All bracketing and underlining is made in comparison to the original patent; not in comparison with the prior amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying markings, compare revised text against original patent text to show deletions and additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper amendment handling and consequences (Form ¶22.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), a supplemental paper correctly proposing amendments is required. A shortened statutory period for response is set to expire ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS (whichever is longer). If patent owner fails to timely correct the informality, the amendment will be held not to be an appropriate response, prosecution of the ex parte reexamination will be terminated, and a reexamination certificate will issue (37 CFR 1.550(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.13 to advise of noncompliant amendments prior to final rejection. After final rejection, do not enter the amendment and inform owner using PTOL 467. Cover sheet PTOL-473 or alternative PTOL-475 available for mailing the notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment entry policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments which comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and are formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b), and contain all fees required, will be entered in the reexamination file pursuant to guidelines in MPEP §2234.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure full compliance with procedural, formatting, marking, support, claim-status, and fee requirements to have amendments entered; otherwise, expect informal responses or non-entry.
